questions.prompt: In Java, what is the contract between equals and hashCode?

options.text: Equal objects must return the same hashCode
hashCode must always return a positive number
Overriding equals makes hashCode unnecessary
Different objects must return different hashCodes

questions.explanation: Breaking this means an object cannot be found in a HashMap it was just put into, because the lookup goes to a different bucket. Unequal objects may share a hash; that is just a collision.

questions.prompt: What does Spring's @Transactional do when placed on a public service method?

options.text: It runs the method on a background thread
It retries the method on any exception
It caches the method's return value
It wraps the call in a database transaction via a proxy

questions.explanation: Spring creates a proxy that opens a transaction before the call and commits or rolls back after. This is why calling the method from inside the same class bypasses it entirely.

questions.prompt: What is the default bean scope in Spring?

options.text: request
session
singleton
prototype

questions.explanation: One instance per container is created and shared. That is why mutable instance fields on a bean are a concurrency bug: every request touches the same object.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a checked and an unchecked exception?

options.text: Unchecked exceptions always terminate the program
Unchecked exceptions cannot be caught
Checked exceptions are thrown only by the JVM
Checked exceptions must be declared or handled at compile time

questions.explanation: Checked exceptions extend Exception and the compiler enforces handling. Unchecked ones extend RuntimeException and represent programming errors that usually should not be caught locally.

questions.prompt: Why does JPA lazy loading often cause an N+1 query problem?

options.text: JPA disables the query cache when lazy is used
Each entity's collection is fetched on first access, one query at a time
Lazy collections are always fetched twice
Lazy loading opens a new connection per entity

questions.explanation: Loading a list of parents is one query; touching each parent's lazy collection in a loop issues one more per parent. A join fetch or an entity graph collapses it back to one.

questions.prompt: What does dependency injection give you over constructing collaborators directly?

options.text: Guaranteed thread safety
Automatic database transactions
Faster object creation at runtime
Dependencies can be swapped, notably for tests

questions.explanation: A class that receives its collaborators does not decide their concrete type, so a test can pass a fake. A class calling new on its dependencies hardcodes them.

questions.prompt: In Java, what does the final keyword mean on a field?

options.text: The field cannot be null
The field is thread-local
The field cannot be reassigned after initialisation
The object it points to becomes immutable

questions.explanation: final fixes the reference, not the object. A final List can still have elements added; only rebinding the variable is prevented.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between ArrayList and LinkedList for random access?

options.text: ArrayList is O(1); LinkedList is O(n)
Both are O(1)
LinkedList is faster because it uses pointers
ArrayList does not support index access

questions.explanation: ArrayList is backed by an array so index access is direct. LinkedList must walk the chain from an end, which is why it loses despite better mid-list insertion.

questions.prompt: What does Spring Boot's auto-configuration actually do?

options.text: It generates your entity classes from the database
It deploys the app to a server automatically
It configures beans based on what is on the classpath
It compiles the application ahead of time

questions.explanation: Conditional configuration classes activate when a library is present and no conflicting bean is defined. Adding a JDBC driver is what silently gives you a configured DataSource.

questions.prompt: Why is String immutable in Java?

options.text: It reduces the size of each String object
It makes string concatenation faster
It is required for Unicode support
It allows safe sharing, caching and use as a hash key

questions.explanation: Immutability makes strings safe to share across threads, allows the string pool, and guarantees a hash key cannot change after insertion. Concatenation in a loop is actually slower for it.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the @RestController annotation?

options.text: It enables database access in the controller
It makes every method transactional
It marks a class as a controller whose returns are serialised as the response body
It restricts the controller to REST clients only

questions.explanation: It combines @Controller and @ResponseBody, so returned objects are serialised to JSON rather than resolved as a view name.

questions.prompt: What happens during Java garbage collection of a young generation?

options.text: All objects in the heap are scanned and compacted
The JVM restarts the application thread pool
Only objects with finalizers are collected
Short-lived objects are collected and survivors are promoted

questions.explanation: Most objects die young, so a minor collection sweeps the young generation cheaply and promotes anything that survives repeatedly to the old generation.

questions.prompt: Why can calling a @Transactional method from another method in the same class skip the transaction?

options.text: The annotation only works on interfaces
Transactions require an explicit commit call
The internal call bypasses the proxy that applies the behaviour
Spring disallows nested transactions

questions.explanation: Spring's default AOP wraps the bean in a proxy. An internal this call never goes through it, so none of the proxy's advice, including transactions, runs.

questions.prompt: What does the Java Stream API's map operation do?

options.text: Filters elements by a predicate
Transforms each element into another value
Groups elements into a Map
Sorts the stream in place

questions.explanation: map applies a function elementwise and returns a new stream. Streams are lazy, so nothing runs until a terminal operation such as collect is invoked.

questions.prompt: What is the practical difference between an interface and an abstract class in modern Java?

options.text: A class may implement many interfaces but extend only one abstract class
Interfaces cannot declare methods
Interfaces cannot be used as types
Abstract classes cannot have constructors

questions.explanation: Since default methods, interfaces can carry behaviour too. The durable difference is single inheritance of state and constructors versus multiple interface implementation.

questions.prompt: Which Spring annotation injects a value from application.properties?

options.text: @Bean
@Value
@Autowired
@Component

questions.explanation: @Value binds a property or expression into a field or parameter. @ConfigurationProperties is the better choice once several related settings are involved.

questions.prompt: What does the volatile keyword guarantee in Java?

options.text: The field is excluded from garbage collection
The operation is atomic for compound updates
The field is written to disk immediately
Writes are visible to other threads, and reads are not cached locally

questions.explanation: volatile fixes visibility and ordering, not atomicity. count++ on a volatile int is still a race, because read-modify-write is three operations.

questions.prompt: Why is HashMap unsafe for concurrent writes?

options.text: It throws an exception on any second write
Concurrent resizing can corrupt its internal structure
It cannot store more than one thread's data
It silently drops all but the first entry

questions.explanation: Simultaneous resize can leave the internal table inconsistent, historically producing infinite loops. ConcurrentHashMap exists for this, with lock striping rather than one global lock.

questions.prompt: What is constructor injection preferred over field injection for?

options.text: It makes dependencies explicit and allows final fields
It speeds up application startup
It avoids the need for component scanning
It is the only way Spring can inject beans

questions.explanation: A constructor states its requirements, cannot be half-built, and permits final fields. Field injection hides dependencies and needs reflection to test without a container.

questions.prompt: What does Optional in Java aim to prevent?

options.text: Unhandled null return values
Concurrent modification during iteration
Memory leaks in long-running services
Class cast exceptions

questions.explanation: Optional makes absence part of the signature so the caller must confront it. Calling get without checking simply reintroduces the same failure with a different exception.

questions.prompt: In Spring Data JPA, what does extending JpaRepository provide?

options.text: Automatic REST endpoints for the entity
CRUD and paging methods without an implementation
Compile-time SQL validation
A second-level cache by default

questions.explanation: Spring generates a proxy implementing the standard operations, and derives queries from method names such as findByEmailAndActiveTrue.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between == and equals for Java objects?

options.text: == compares references; equals compares content if overridden
== cannot be used on objects at all
equals compares references; == compares content
They behave identically for all objects

questions.explanation: == asks whether two variables point at the same object. equals asks whether they are meaningfully equal, but only if the class overrides it; Object's default is reference equality.

questions.prompt: What is a memory leak in a long-running Java service most often caused by?

options.text: Using primitives instead of wrapper types
Objects still referenced from a long-lived collection or cache
Failing to call System.gc regularly
Creating too many short-lived objects

questions.explanation: Java cannot collect anything still reachable. An unbounded static map or a listener never unregistered keeps objects alive indefinitely, which is a leak in every practical sense.

questions.prompt: Why should an entity's equals not be based on its generated database id alone?

options.text: Ids change every time the row is updated
Database ids are not unique
The id is null before the entity is persisted
JPA forbids overriding equals on entities

questions.explanation: A new entity has a null id, so two unsaved entities compare equal and behave badly in a Set. A business key, or careful null handling, is required.

questions.prompt: What does Spring Security's filter chain do with an incoming request?

options.text: It validates the JSON schema of the payload
It passes the request through ordered filters that authenticate and authorise it
It rewrites the URL to a canonical form
It encrypts the request body before the controller sees it

questions.explanation: A servlet filter chain runs before the controller, establishing the security context or rejecting the request. Understanding filter order is what makes custom authentication work.
